- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.4) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for volatility.  
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes; apply a 1–3 day lag correction: if price spiked 3–5% in last 2–3 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.  
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, consider mean reversion bias — reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overshoots in early periods (first 5–7 days) — cap forecast at 10–15% below recent 18-day high if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings (e.g., +0.4, -0.3, +0.4), model tends to misalign with sentiment cycles — adjust forecast to match sentiment direction with 1–2 day delay.
